answer: No, your records show no blood clot in your lungs. On 8 July 2025 you had a CT scan of your chest done to look for a lung clot (a pulmonary embolism). The report says there was no pulmonary embolism and that your lungs were clear. A blood test taken that day, the D-dimer, was slightly raised. D-dimer can be raised for many reasons, so it is a screening test, and the scan is what settled the question. Your doctors recorded the chest pain you had at that time as chest wall pain, which was marked resolved on 22 July 2025. The records do not show any later blood clot in your lungs or legs. They only go up to mid-October 2026, so if you have had chest pain, breathlessness or leg swelling since then, tell your doctor.
short: Summer 2025 CT angiography of the chest (8 July 2025) showed no pulmonary embolism and clear lungs; the same-day D-dimer was mildly raised, and the chest pain was recorded as chest wall pain, resolved 22 July 2025. No later lung or leg clot appears in records retrieved 15 Oct 2026.

items.says: Your summer 2025 chest CT found no blood clot in your lungs.
items.why: The CT was done specifically to look for a lung clot, and the report says there was none and the lungs were clear. Your problem list also marks the pulmonary embolism diagnosis as ruled out.

facts.says: CT angiography of the chest report: no pulmonary embolism, lungs clear.
facts.name: CT angiography chest (pulmonary embolism protocol)
facts.quote: No pulmonary embolism. Lungs are clear. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.

facts.says: Pulmonary embolism recorded as ruled out on the problem list.
facts.name: Pulmonary embolism

knowledge.says: A CT pulmonary angiogram is the standard test for confirming or excluding a lung clot, so a clear report on that test is a reliable negative for that date.
knowledge.guideline: Use of CT pulmonary angiography to exclude pulmonary embolism when D-dimer is raised (NICE NG158 / ESC PE guidance).

items.says: A blood test taken the same day was mildly raised, which was a screening result that the scan then answered.
items.why: D-dimer is a sensitive but non-specific test for clotting. A raised value prompts imaging, and it does not confirm a clot on its own.

facts.says: D-dimer result 0.92 mg/L FEU, flagged high (reference 0.49 or less).
facts.name: D-dimer

knowledge.says: A raised D-dimer is common with many conditions, so it needs imaging to decide whether a clot is present.
knowledge.guideline: NICE NG158 (D-dimer followed by CTPA when raised in suspected PE).

items.says: The chest pain you had then was recorded as chest wall pain, and it resolved by 22 July 2025.
items.why: The problem list gives chest wall pain as the working diagnosis from 8 July 2025, marked resolved and abated on 22 July 2025, after the scan had ruled out a clot.

facts.says: Chest wall pain, onset 8 July 2025, resolved and abated 22 July 2025.
facts.name: Chest wall pain

knowledge.says: Chest wall pain is a common, usually musculoskeletal cause of chest pain once a serious cause such as a clot has been excluded.
knowledge.guideline: NICE CKS chest pain guidance (non-cardiac chest pain assessment).

items.why: The problem list and the reports and procedures in the pod contain no later pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis entry, so the absence is limited to the period covered by the records.

knowledge.guideline: No specific guideline; general principle that a single provider's records can be incomplete.
